title: Harmony Science Academy Cuts Ribbon on New 3D Anatomy Table
excerpt: Harmony Science Academy celebrated a new piece of science equipment Wednesday with a ribbon-cutting ceremony for an interactive 3D anatomy table — technology that lets students zoom in and explore the human body up close.
content:
Harmony Science Academy celebrated the arrival of a new piece of science equipment Wednesday with a ribbon-cutting ceremony for an interactive 3D anatomy table.

The advanced technology gives students a closer look at human anatomy and helps them better understand how the body works. Students can zoom in on the table to explore the parts of the human body and the information they need for their curriculum.

Science and STEM teacher Mr. Sunia said the table will be used to teach students about human anatomy, starting with the school’s middle school to medical school program. Students begin in sixth grade and continue through seventh and eighth grade in the program, then move on to high school, where they follow a biomedical pathway and can earn high school credit while still in middle school.

Students at the ceremony said the table will help them grow in their medical careers, giving them a chance to see the human body in detail and explore how it works — and to feel more inspired toward the medical field.

The school celebrated the new table as a hands-on way to bring science lessons to life for its students.
